description:
Development and test executables keep their debug information outside the linked executable, so each test binary stops carrying its own copy of the workspace's debug sections.

## Background

The dev and test profiles use `debug = "line-tables-only"`. Each of the about 13 active test executables is still roughly 115 MB, and about 75% of that is debug information. For `cli_issue` this is `.debug_str` 25.7 MB, `.debug_info` 19.4 MB and `.debug_line` 18.3 MB, against 16.1 MB of code, duplicated into every executable. The build-budget step reported `active-executables=14 bytes=1716158664` against a 2 GiB budget on 2026-11-04.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The dev and test profiles declare `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Active test-executable bytes, as reported by the build-budget step, fall by at least 40% from the before value measured on the same commit without the change. Both values and the measurement commands are recorded in the build-budget README.
- [hard] REQ-03: A panicking test still prints a backtrace with source file and line numbers for workspace frames, shown by a test or a recorded reproduction.
- [hard] REQ-04: The executable-bytes budget in `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` is lowered to the measured after value plus at most 10% headroom, and the README derives it.
- [hard] REQ-05: The build profile policy test asserts the setting, and the existing suites pass.
title: Test executables keep debug information out of the linked binary
